newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.

text.p: * Lower Chamber of Deputies' foreign policy commission met Theodossis Georgiou, chairman Greece's NATO and European cooperation association.

* The Romanian delegation to Kiev -- led by foreign ministry secretary of state Dumitru Ciausu -- is empowered to negotiate any proposal by Ukraine that could lead to the signature of the bilateral treaty, foreign ministry spokeswoman Gilda Lazar said.

* Foreign Minister Adrian Severin is expected to meet Romania's exiled King Michael next Monday -- during the former monarch's five-day visit to Romania due to start on Friday -- to discuss plans to entrust the king with a mission "of good offices" to woo support for his country from Europe's constitutional monarchies, Lazar said.
* Michael will be handed a new passport upon arrival at Romania's Otopeni airport.
* The European Union's external relations commissioner Hans van den Broek is expected to visit over March 5-7 to discuss Romania's progress towards joining the EU as a member.
* Senator Viorel Catarama met the Chamber of Deputies' economic commission to present a draft law to amend foreign investment rules, allowing foreign investors to buy land.
The Senate had previously passed the law.
* National radio's administration board asked for a 110.9 billion lei in the 1997 budget allocation. The radio faces overstaffing and a drop in ratings.

* Sidex SA steel mill in Galati will no longer be able to transport its raw materials and products on rails starting Friday, due to debts worth over 50 billion lei to the country's railway authority, Transport Minister Traian Basescu said.
He said steel mills in Hunedoara and Calarasi were in a similar situation.
* Prices of urban transport rose in Bucharest to 700 lei for a trip, from a previous 400 lei. A trip on the capital's subway would cost 800 lei, up from 300 lei previously.
